title: Only such cult is lawful toward the blessed as suits an absent creature
source_text: XXI. Caeterum ut jam videamus qua in re consistat honor, quem Beatis in caelo spiritibus, sive hominum, sive Angelorum, deberi fatentur Scholae Reformatae Doctores, ante omnia in genere statuunt nullum cultum licite illis exhiberi posse, quam qui competit creaturae absenti, aut quae instar absentis est, & cum qua nullum nobis est mutuum commercium.
pass_a_gloss: But so that we may now see in what the honor consists which the doctors of the Reformed School confess is owed to the blessed spirits in heaven, whether of men or of angels, they lay down before all things in general that no cult can lawfully be shown them except that which belongs to an absent creature, or one that is as if absent, and with which we have no mutual commerce.
pass_b_english: The next question is what honor the Reformed actually grant the blessed, whether human or angelic.
Their general rule is that nothing may be shown them beyond what fits a creature who is absent, or as good as absent.
There is no mutual commerce with such a creature on which a richer cult could rest.

choices.why: The limit is lawful cult, not a denial that any honor is due.
rejected: the same cult as to the present living
